text:
A tired river took shelter in the shade

of the sweet trees..., of the trees

so serene they do not have to run...

And there it remained in the grace of a bend.


Now the backwater is made. Tiny roots

fasten it to the shore of its soul:

Reflecting lights and shadows,

they fall asleep with a dream without distances...


It is midday: Across the blue sky

a dove passes...

The river is so still

that the hawk, hidden among the branches,

no longer knows for an instant

where to stretch its flight with its claw:

Toward the fine bird of the air

or toward the bird, finer still, of the water...

translation.title: The Backwater
translation.editorial_note: The translation follows the river as it becomes a still backwater where sky and reflection momentarily confuse the hawk.
